messages.subject: Executive Value Proposition | FAB | Sustainability, Government Relations & Strategic Execution
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Bashir,

I am writing to share a strategic value proposition prepared specifically for First Abu Dhabi Bank as FAB expands its global franchise while deepening sustainable and transition finance, client engagement and climate-related governance.

I currently serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department, at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My mandate spans senior government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance, strategic partnerships, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory within a capital-intensive multinational operating environment. I work across public institutions, communities, technical teams and senior management to convert external expectations into accountable execution.

FAB's current direction aligns closely with my experience. The Group is operating at more than AED 1.4 trillion in assets, with a substantial international balance sheet, while embedding transition considerations across operations, client relationships and capital allocation. My background is most relevant where sustainability strategy, government relationships, operating evidence, executive governance and international market execution intersect.

Rather than send a conventional CV alone, I have attached a FAB-specific strategic value brief. It identifies areas where my experience could support the Group across ESG execution, transition-finance evidence, institutional stakeholder strategy, international market readiness and executive issue governance. The document also includes a 90-180 day action framework and my three-page executive CV.

I would value a confidential discussion if you see alignment within Group Sustainability, Corporate Affairs, Government Relations, Strategy, International Banking or selected client-transition and portfolio initiatives.

Kind regards,

Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director | AGM Inc., Zijin Mining Group
Georgetown, Guyana
+592 608 4735
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposition for FAB
strategic_brief.prepared_for_title: Executive Vice President and Group Chief Sustainability Officer
strategic_brief.executive_summary: FAB is scaling a global banking franchise while embedding sustainability and transition considerations across operations, client relationships and capital allocation. That combination creates a growing need for disciplined execution at the intersection of ESG, government relations, stakeholder expectations, operating evidence and executive governance. My value proposition is to bring an operator's perspective to that interface. As Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, I lead country-facing government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social responsibility, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory in a capital-intensive multinational environment. I would bring FAB practical experience in translating external commitments into evidence, accountable ownership and cross-functional action, with particular relevance to client transition, regulated-market engagement, international growth and executive sustainability governance.
strategic_brief.company_context: FAB entered the second half of 2026 from a position of exceptional scale and resilience. Its H1 2026 results reported AED 19.50 billion in operating income, AED 13.20 billion in profit before tax, AED 10.73 billion in net profit and total assets of AED 1.41 trillion. International assets reached AED 437 billion, or 31 percent of Group assets, reinforcing FAB's global operating profile. At the same time, FAB's 2026 Transition Pathways Update states that sustainable and transition finance activities contributed to nearly four million tonnes of avoided CO2 emissions in 2025 and emphasizes disciplined decarbonisation, structured client engagement and scaled sustainable finance. This combination of international growth, large-scale capital allocation and transition leadership creates a strong need for high-quality ESG evidence, institutional stakeholder management and consistent execution across business lines and markets.

opportunities.title: Transition Strategy to Operating Evidence
opportunities.rationale: FAB's transition agenda spans financed emissions, client engagement, sustainable finance and its own operations. As the programme scales, leadership confidence depends on traceable evidence, clear ownership and consistent review processes that connect headline commitments with underlying operating data, client actions and measurable outcomes across business units and jurisdictions.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support governance structures that link commitments to source evidence, named owners, milestones and concise executive reporting. My experience includes coordinating a carbon-accounting proof of concept using physical operating records across fuel, electricity, explosives, material movement, production and refinery data to strengthen traceability and review readiness.

opportunities.title: Government and Institutional Stakeholder Strategy
opportunities.rationale: As a global bank headquartered in Abu Dhabi, FAB operates across regulatory, government, sovereign and institutional interfaces that influence market access, client strategy, sustainable finance and public-policy alignment. Structured stakeholder architecture helps leadership anticipate external dependencies and coordinate engagement before policy or regulatory developments become execution risks.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would map priority authorities, regulators, investment institutions and strategic partners across selected markets and establish relationship plans, executive briefs, commitment trackers and escalation routes. My current role requires continuous senior engagement with multiple public institutions where trust, timing and disciplined follow-through directly affect operating outcomes.

opportunities.title: International Market and Client Transition Readiness
opportunities.rationale: With nearly one-third of Group assets international, FAB's growth and client-transition agenda increasingly crosses different regulatory, political and stakeholder environments. International execution benefits from early visibility of country-level ESG expectations, local policy direction, government priorities and institutional sensitivities alongside the commercial and credit case.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would develop practical country and client-readiness frameworks integrating regulatory pathways, stakeholder analysis, ESG expectations and executive decision support. My multinational operating experience focuses on translating external requirements into coordinated action across corporate, technical and country teams in complex regulated environments.

opportunities.title: Executive ESG Issues and Reputation Governance
opportunities.rationale: Banks face increasing scrutiny around sustainable finance claims, transition credibility, social impact, financed emissions and client-sector exposure. Sensitive matters often require rapid coordination across sustainability, risk, legal, communications, business and senior leadership. A disciplined issues framework improves factual accuracy, ownership and response quality while reducing avoidable reputation and governance risk.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish concise executive issue briefs, stakeholder-risk registers, evidence trackers and escalation protocols for selected high-exposure matters. I routinely coordinate regulator-facing and reputation-sensitive issues across operations, HSE, environment, legal, finance, procurement, HR, security and senior management, with emphasis on accuracy, accountability and closure.

days_0_30: Confirm the sustainability, client-transition, international-market or stakeholder workstreams where additional execution support would create the strongest value.
Map priority regulators, government entities, institutional stakeholders, client dependencies and internal owners against live strategic priorities.
Review ESG evidence, management reporting, stakeholder intelligence and escalation processes to identify gaps and decision bottlenecks.
days_31_60: Select three to five priority pilots based on strategic importance, stakeholder complexity and executive sponsorship.
Build integrated plans with clear objectives, owners, evidence requirements, milestones and escalation thresholds.
Create a concise executive dashboard covering transition commitments, external dependencies, unresolved issues and partnership opportunities.
days_61_90: Launch pilot stakeholder and ESG-governance workstreams with agreed executive sponsors.
Connect selected transition commitments to source data, action owners and management review.
Capture repeatable lessons suitable for wider Group or market deployment.
days_91_180: Scale effective practices into a common toolkit for transition governance, institutional engagement and international market readiness.
Measure impact through issue closure, evidence quality, decision-cycle time, stakeholder outcomes and implementation progress.
Institutionalize a reporting cadence giving leadership early visibility of material ESG and external dependencies.

potential_impact: Stronger traceability between transition commitments, underlying evidence and accountable implementation.
Earlier visibility of government, regulatory and institutional dependencies across priority markets and client sectors.
More consistent executive decision support on sustainability and reputation-sensitive matters.
Improved readiness for cross-border client-transition and market-growth initiatives.
A repeatable governance framework connecting sustainability strategy with practical operating execution.
background_relevance: Current Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, with country-facing responsibility spanning government and regulatory relations, ESG, social responsibility, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive communications.
Leads senior institutional engagement across mining, environment, energy, aviation, labour, standards, taxation, trade, investment and social-performance matters.
Coordinates sensitive external commitments and issues across operations, HSE, environment, legal, HR, finance, procurement, security, aviation and technical teams.
Supports stakeholder governance around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage.
Coordinated a 2026 carbon-accounting proof of concept using physical operating data to strengthen emissions traceability and review readiness.
Brings 12+ years across multinational mining, regulated financial services and commercial operations, supported by an MBA and international executive-development exposure.
